title: Fix Clone Snapshot State Machine Bug

timeline.message:
Fix Clone Snapshot State Machine Bug

This fixes a left over from #65042 where if a clone
was initially put in the cluster state before another clone
but then initialized after the other clone already finished its shard clones,
a broken snapshot state would be reached where the first clone
would be queued before the almost finished clone.

closes #67871
timeline.author: Armin Braun

timeline.body:
This fixes a left over from #65042 where if a clone
was initially put in the cluster state before another clone
but then initialized after the other clone already finished its shard clones,
a broken snapshot state would be reached where the first clone
would be queued before the almost finished clone.

closes #67871

This is admittedly pretty :facepalm: but we don't have a clean way of expressing just a one-time block here. The dependency on another block is due to how the `blockExecution` loop works (doesn't play well with one-time actions).

reply.body: Could you add a reference to `MockRepository#blockExecution` in the javadoc? It took me a bit to understand how the dependency on another block was enforced.

timeline.body:
This broke because for `SUCCESS` state shards we would not queue up the shard clone (rightfully so) but would still have the `SUCCESS` state clone that is just about to finalize after the current clone, tripping assertions (and without them leading to stuck clone operations).
Should have never had the `queuedShards` condition here, it just creates all kinds of trouble to not simply move

This is pretty close to a ">blocker" I think as it can lead to a stuck snapshot state machine (though it's not a new issue and cloning is still very rarely used I suppose). We can discuss this tomorrow.
